name: s3_sixway
title: With six columns to choose from, the NLA still separates first from late but never picks columns 4 to 6
caption: Exp 17: table-column items re-scored over all six column values (160 exp 13 selection items: 80 first-cell, 80 late-cell with true column 4-6). A and B: which column the NLA's phrasing 'The current cell is in the {v} column of the table' ranks highest; it picks 'first' on 75 of 80 first-cell items and never picks columns 4-6, even when they are true. C: first vs late AUROC from log-sum-exp over each class's candidates (Oracle Lens: column-number bullets; J-lens: column words), 95% bootstrap CI clustered by passage (2,000 resamples). Six-way top-1 for the NLA is 0.47 [0.39, 0.55] against chance 0.17. Caveat: the 94% is a prompted argmax, not free readouts; with a per-candidate prior subtracted, late items do go to columns 4-6 (45 of 80).
